subject: Request: Custom SLA addendum + order form language for Aurelia Health
messages:
From: Claire Beaumont <procurement@aureliahealth.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-01-11T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: SLA and order form questions ahead of procurement review

Hi Irene,

Thanks for the product overview last week — the performance numbers looked promising. Our procurement and security teams have a couple of asks before we can route a purchase order: primarily a tailored uptime exhibit and a short appendix to the order form that states latency targets for inference calls in our region (us-west).

Attached are our initial redlines and a short matrix of throughput/latency evidence requests. High level asks: 99.9% availability for the dedicated instance, a 200ms p95 inference latency target for single-turn text-gen for sequences under 512 tokens, and a defined fallback behavior if the dedicated pool is unavailable.

Can you confirm whether Redwood can provide an SLA addendum + order form language that covers this? Also if you have recent runbook/evidence artifacts we can attach for procurement, that would speed internal review.

Attachments: Aurelia_SLA_redlines_v1.pdf; uptime-evidence-matrix.xlsx

Best,
Claire Beaumont
Senior Procurement Manager
Aurelia Health Partners

Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwoodinference.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwoodinference.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-01-11T11:03:00-08:00
Subject: Re: SLA and order form questions ahead of procurement review

Claire — thanks for sending the redlines and the matrix. We can accommodate most of these asks but want to confirm a few implementation details before we draft formal language:

- Availability: 99.9% on Dedicated is feasible with a tailored addendum; we typically propose an uptime exhibit with monthly uptime calculation and credits tied to the Order Form.
- Latency: 200ms p95 for <512 tokens in us-west is aggressive but achievable for optimized models and right instance sizing. We need to confirm the model variant you intend to run (open model vs larger family) and expected QPS. Marcus can run a quick perf check against the sample prompt set in your matrix.
- Fallbacks: we can add automatic fallback to a compatible model variant in a separate region or a hosted tier; we should capture the routing priority and expected mode of failure in the addendum.

Action items I propose: Marcus will provide performance evidence (p95/p99) and recommended instance sizing; Ben will draft Order Form language and an uptime exhibit; Karthik, can you take an initial pass at legal-friendly warranty/credit language and point to any non-starters?

Reply-all and I’ll coordinate a one-hour alignment call if that helps speed procurement approval.

Thanks — Irene

Subject: Re: SLA and order form questions ahead of procurement review

Irene / team — I ran the sample prompt set Claire attached against our c6-dedicated profile (quantized 4-bit) and an optimized model variant. Quick summary:

- p95 latency (single-turn, <512 tokens): 170-190ms in us-west under 10 QPS sustained. p99 sits around 260ms.
- With autoscaling to the next instance size, sustained QPS > 30 will push p95 above 250ms.
- Cache priming (prefix caching for stable prompts) can reduce observed p95 by ~20% for repeat workloads.

I’ve attached the perf snapshots and a short recommendation: include a note in the order form that the 200ms p95 target applies to single-turn inference under a defined usage profile (QPS <= 20, model variant = REW-Opt-1). If the customer intends higher QPS or different models, we should either (a) size Dedicated differently or (b) set a higher p95 target and offer credits only when the workload meets the documented profile.

Attachments: uptime-evidence-matrix.xlsx (updated), perf-snapshots-usw.csv

—Marcus
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwoodinference.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwoodinference.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwoodinference.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-01-13T09:08:00-08:00
Subject: Re: SLA and order form questions ahead of procurement review

Team — initial legal take below (high level):

- Availability & credits: we can accept a 99.9% availability metric in a tailored exhibit with monthly measurement and capped credits (e.g., service credits up to 30% of monthly fees for severe breaches). Avoid unlimited liability and keep remedies to credits or termination right after repeated breaches (3 consecutive months).
- Latency target: ok to reference a 200ms p95 but we must tie it to the documented workload profile and a provisioning clause. Suggest language: "Latency SLOs apply to requests that meet the workload profile described in the Order Form (model variant, sequence length, and QPS)." This prevents the customer from claiming credits when they run a heavier workload.
- Fallbacks and cross-region fallthrough: define expected routing priority and any data locality constraints — if the customer requires strict regional-only processing, fallback to other regions may be disallowed.

I’ll draft sample warranty and credit clauses for Ben to fold into the Order Form. Ben — can you accept a 48-hour review turnaround once I send the draft?

Karthik
Senior Counsel, Contracts | Redwood Inference

Claire / Tom — thanks for the detailed redlines; we reviewed and put together a short package for procurement: a proposed SLA addendum (attached), an Order Form excerpt that captures the workload profile, and performance artifacts. High level summary: 99.9% monthly availability with capped credits, 200ms p95 latency scoped to the documented workload (QPS <= 20, model = REW-Opt-1), and automatic fallback behavior defined when Dedicated capacity is unavailable (fallback to hosted tier with notification and no credit).

I’ve attached the proposed files for your review. If this aligns, we can convert the Order Form excerpt into a DocuSign envelope and I’ll engage Revenue Ops to prepare the final purchase path. If procurement prefers stronger fallthrough guarantees or regional-only processing, let us know and we’ll surface the commercial impact.

Attachments: Proposed_SLA_Addendum_Aurelia.pdf; Aurelia_OrderForm_Excerpt.docx; perf-snapshots-usw.csv
